text:
maria: Heads up — noticed an odd scale-down yesterday in us-west1-gpu where CA kicked nodes but pods didn't move. cost spike + some 503s. Anyone see this?

devon: saw alerts. CA logs show scaleDown in progress but kubectl drain hung on PDBs. I grabbed a few logs.

maria: paste the drain snippet?

devon: ```kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
W1203 10:12:34.123 drain.go:183] evicting pod kube-system/monitor-agent: blocked by pdb/my-gpu-pipeline-pdb (minAvailable:1, current:1)
error: unable to drain node
```

liam: ah — the trainer pod is backed by a PDB with minAvailable:1. It's a long-running, local-checkpoint pod so it's not evictable. CA waits until it's evictable or until max-unready-percentage allows another node removal.

maria: but we expected CA to fallback to lower tier (preemptible -> regular) or skip GPU node to avoid API errors. Instead it kept trying and triggered rollout retries upstream.

ops-jen: two things: (1) some pods are missing priorityClass so kubelet treats them as default, can't be force-evicted if PDB says minAvailable; (2) we have cluster-autoscaler config with --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m and --max-empty-bulk-delete=2, but no safe-to-evict annotations.

liam: short-term mitigation: mark the trainer pod with annotation `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true` but only if replica >1 or we can rebuild from checkpoint.

maria: Can we define a priorityClass for GPU batch jobs (e.g., gpu-batch-critical vs gpu-batch-evictable) and set PDB minAvailable accordingly?

devon: yes — recommendation: create PriorityClass with value 1000 for non-evictable, 100 for evictable. Then update deployments/statefulsets that can lose a replica to the lower class. Also adjust PDBs from minAvailable:1 to minAvailable:0 where acceptable so drain progresses.

liam: sample PriorityClass YAML:
```yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: gpu-evictable
value: 100
description: "Evictable GPU workload for scale-down"
globalDefault: false
```

ops-jen: Another pattern: instead of changing PDBs, add a CA-safe-probe pre-check that annotates pods ephemeral if they've completed checkpoint successfully. We use a small sidecar that writes `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true` after checkpoint completion.

maria: That avoids PDB churn. Good. What about daemonsets and local storage? NVidia device plugin is a DaemonSet so drain uses --ignore-daemonsets. But some training pods write local checkpoints to /train/checkpoint and we set emptyDir so `--delete-local-data` needed. Risky.

devon: for local data we should ensure trainers either push checkpoints to GCS on schedule or write to persistent volumes. For scale-down safety, prefer PV-backed storage so we can evict without losing progress.

liam: operational checklist suggestion for GPU scale-down:
- Tag pools with node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=gpu
- CA exclude list: add `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false`? (we prefer explicit annotation)
- Have controllers set `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict` after checkpoint
- Use a lower PDB minAvailable for non-critical jobs
- Define PriorityClasses and default to evictable for most batch workloads

maria: Is there a way to make CA prefer draining non-gpu nodes first if region capacity is tight? We saw CA trying to drain GPU nodes in one zone even though other zones had empties.

devon: CA has `--balance-similar-node-groups` and `--expander=least-waste` options. But zone packing + podTopologyConstraints can force GPU placements. We should also set nodeGroup metadata to prefer draining spot/preemptible pools first. CA supports `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false` but we can annotate node groups as `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/disable-scale-down` for pools we never want drained unexpectedly.

ops-jen: For cost: we run some GPU pools as spot/preemptible — we need an eviction strategy that recognizes preemptible churn. Suggest: a small reserved GPU pool for critical low-latency workloads, and a larger spot pool for opportunistic training with aggressive evictable settings.

maria: Action items?

devon: 1) Create gpu-evictable PriorityClass + update non-critical controllers — I can PR.
2) Add CA annotation pattern + sidecar example doc — liam?
3) Audit PDBs in us-west1-gpu for minAvailable:1 and flag those we can relax — ops-jen.

liam: I'll draft the sidecar and a short runbook for safe drain (`kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 --force` is last resort). Include sample script to annotate after checkpoint: `kubectl annotate pod $POD cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true`

ops-jen: I'll also add a healthcheck to our deployment pipeline that warns if a new GPU workload lacks a PriorityClass or PDB.

oncall-bot: incident-note created: "gpu-scale-down-blocked-by-pdbs" assigned to eng-infra. Link: https://issue-tracker/infra/3241

maria: perfect. Thanks team — let's get PRs small and staged so CA behavior improves before next cost spike. :thumbsup:
